summary:
Farmers worldwide face an escalating dilemma: shifting frost windows, intensifying heatwaves, and erratic rainfall make multi-generational intuition unreliable, trapping growers in defensive, high-water monocultures. Trying an unfamiliar crop rotation can restore soil health and save water, but gambling on the wrong crop risks total stand loss and financial ruin. Meanwhile, NASA captures petabytes of open Earth observations that could guide these decisions, but orbital data remains locked in complex scientific formats that never reach the field.

We built Field Shift, an open-source, client-side decision-support tool that bridges 35 years of NASA Earth observations directly to field-level seasonal management. By harmonizing 7 NASA missions and calibrating them against local weather stations, Field Shift allows producers to outline any field parcel, set their own priorities (conserving water, keeping soil covered, nitrogen fixation, cash flow), and test multi-year rotation scenarios in under 5 milliseconds. The tool provides transparent mathematical evidence and local agronomist checklists—comparing options without ever dictating what to plant.
details:
1. What does your project do, and how does it work?

Field Shift is an interactive, browser-based decision-support workspace designed to help agricultural producers and local extension officers navigate climate volatility through crop rotation.

Instead of treating crop selection as a static recommendation, Field Shift operates as an interactive flight simulator for the field:

  1. Interactive Field Selection: A user selects an agricultural basin or sketches their own field boundary anywhere on a satellite basemap.
  2. Multi-Mission Zonal Ingestion: The system instantly queries a precomputed 140 m raster atlas fusing 7 NASA Earth observation missions, displaying the parcel's 35-year climate history, soil moisture anomalies, vegetative greenness cycles, and terrain slope.
  3. The 12-Month Rotation Ring: The parcel's annual canopy dynamics are projected onto a circular 365-day wheel. Living crop cover is traced in colored arcs, while vulnerable bare-soil windows appear as empty gaps.
  4. 3-Vector Stress Calendar: The platform cross-references seasonal bare-ground periods (NDVI<0.25NDVI < 0.25NDVI<0.25) against historical high-intensity rainfall events (GPM IMERG), wind erosion months, and peak heat stress windows (NASA POWER).
  5. Deterministic Scenario Exploration: The farmer sets their own operational priorities using 8 adjustable weights and 3 hard feasibility constraints (irrigation water allocation caps, machinery availability, and guaranteed buyer access). In less than 5 milliseconds, the system evaluates alternative multi-year crop rotations, displaying ranked strategies alongside auditable point breakdowns and risks.

2. What benefits does it have, and what is the intended impact?

  • Risk-Free Exploration: Farmers can test alternative cropping sequences against historic droughts, shifting frost dates, and water cutbacks on screen before spending a dollar on seed or expending limited water rights.
  • Aquifer and Soil Conservation: Crop diversification breaks autotoxicity cycles, adds biological nitrogen, and eliminates critical post-harvest bare-fallow windows that drive topsoil erosion.
    • Arid Alluvial Basins (Nevada High Desert): Proved 118 mm/yr118\text{ mm/yr}118 mm/yr (~17%) irrigation savings (15M to 59M liters15\text{M to }59\text{M liters}15M to 59M liters per center pivot) by transitioning continuous alfalfa into winter triticale and sorghum-sudangrass.
    • Intensive Breadbasket Plains (Punjab): Proved ∼650 mm/yr\sim 650\text{ mm/yr}∼650 mm/yr irrigation reduction by replacing summer puddled rice with maize-wheat-moong rotations.
    • Tropical Canal Deltas (Cauvery Delta): Demonstrated canal water stabilization by replacing double-paddy with single Samba rice and residual moisture pulses.
  • Responsible Deployment: Every strategy card includes a mandatory "Verify with Local Agronomist" checklist covering herbicide carryover plant-back restrictions, soil salinity thresholds, and seed availability.

3. How is your project creative and unique?

  • Rejection of Black-Box AI: Commercial agricultural technology often relies on opaque neural networks that attempt to predict unvalidated yields, eroding farmer trust. Field Shift uses transparent, deterministic Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) backed by FAO-56 and USDA standards. Every score is fully auditable.
  • The "Rotation Ring" Abstraction: Multi-year crop sequences are complex. Visualizing them as an annual circular clock allows growers to immediately spot bare-soil gaps and water demand peaks at a glance.
  • 100% Client-Side Architecture: The entire scoring engine runs locally in compiled TypeScript within the user's browser. It requires zero server infrastructure, eliminates server latency (<5 ms<5\text{ ms}<5 ms response), protects farmer privacy, and works reliably in low-bandwidth rural settings.

4. What tools, coding languages, and software did you use?

  • Frontend & Visualization: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL JS (satellite map rendering), Recharts (climate time-series), and Canvas API (custom Rotation Ring rendering).
  • Data Harmonization & Pipeline: Python 3.12, GDAL/Rasterio, Shapely, NumPy, Pandas, and Parquet.
  • Quality Assurance & Verification: Automated Pytest suite with 49 tests. This includes a strict parity testing engine (test_parity.py) that runs both the Python reference model and the browser’s TypeScript engine on identical fields, verifying that scores match to 3 decimal places and output text matches word-for-word.
